newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan, Italy pledge to boost cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan, Italy pledge to boost cooperation.

text.p: Kazakhstan and Italy signed a friendship and cooperation treaty on Monday, declaring the start of a new stage in their political and economic ties.

"This treaty will open a new stage in our relations," Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev told a news briefing after the document was signed by Kazakh Foreign Minister Kasymzhomart Tokayev and Italian Deputy Foreign Minister Piero Fassino.
Nazarbayev said Italy was the first European country which recognised Kazakhstan as a sovereign and independent state after the Soviet Union collapsed in late 1991.

"Italy wants to be a friend of the people of Kazakhstan," said Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, who arrived in the resource-rich former Soviet republic on a three-day visit on Sunday and is accompanied by a group of Italian businessmen.
Nazarbayev said Kazakhstan would be interested in Italy's assistance in developing small and medium-sized businesses.
Italian companies are already involved in developing the Central Asian state's oil and gas riches.

Agip SpA is part of a multinational consortium which plans to build a pipeline to export Kazakh crude oil to international markets from the giant Tengiz oilfield via the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
Official figures show Italy is Kazakhstan's seventh largest trading partner. Nazarbayev said that mutual trade reached almost $240 million last year.
